findings.detail: Earlier question M1-S46-T1 uses the same scene: a nightly CI batch that generates test suites per source file. It has the same failure: results are matched to files by position in the results list, so test suites land on the wrong files. Option B gives the same fix, reading custom_id instead of position, so the same reasoning leads to the answer. Option C repeats M1's wrong option, order-based matching by position. Option E echoes M3-S12-T1's wrong option of moving to the synchronous API. Only the chunk-ID detail in option A is new, which is not enough of a different problem.

blind_answer.reason: Batch results are not guaranteed to come back in submission order, so position-based matching is unreliable. The fix is to identify failed files by reading the custom_id on each failed result. Each chunk should also get a custom_id built from the original file's custom_id plus a chunk number, so every chunk result can be mapped back to its source file. Option C still relies on position. Option D would hit the context limit again. Option E drops the batch API's cost savings and doesn't fix the correlation design.
